International research collaborations in cutting-edge fields such as AI or cybersecurity are important—but can sometimes pose risks.

This new paper offers a framework for understanding and managing risks in science and technology research partnerships: bit.ly/4tQZd5y
New report on safeguarding crop production in the U.S. Corn Belt against emerging biological, environmental, and societal risks: bit.ly/4e9nJKg
New Q&A with RAND's Scott Savitz, a specialist in naval operations and technologies, and an expert in mine warfare: bit.ly/4dECLqc

Israel's international isolation is deepening fast.

What can stop this slide? RAND's Shira Efron discusses: nytimes.com/2026/05/28/opini…

Stricter school cell phone policies are associated with less student phone use during class. But even the strictest policies don't completely stop student phone use.

New report: bit.ly/4uSyFBM
In this new Q&A, RAND's Scott Savitz discusses the threat of naval mines and the challenge of clearing the Strait of Hormuz: bit.ly/42PFZlF

Without proper safeguards, international research partnerships may serve as avenues for espionage, economic exploitation, or unethical applications of research.

New resource on research security in science and technology: bit.ly/4tVyUv1

"One of the things that we've learned with cannabis legalization is that … if you're prohibiting [a substance] and you want to do something different, you don't necessarily need to jump all the way to the for-profit commercial model." bit.ly/499UwfG

What is the scale and sophistication of the mine threat in the Strait of Hormuz? And how hard will it be to clear a passage that's perceived as safe?

New Q&A with RAND's Scott Savitz: bit.ly/3POsWxU

A new RAND study finds that stricter school cell phone policies are associated with less student phone use in class, but even the most restrictive policies don't completely stop students from checking their phones. bit.ly/3PC9owG

New findings from our survey of unsheltered residents in three Los Angeles neighborhoods: Skid Row, Venice, and Hollywood ⤵️ 
bit.ly/3PREwbD
China faces a problem that could strain its government, undermine its security, and sap its economic energy: It isn't having enough babies. bit.ly/4mOI22x

The risk that even a few Iranian naval mines have landed in the Strait of Hormuz has paralyzed shipping traffic in one of the world's most vital waterways.

RAND's Scott Savitz discusses what it might take to clear these weapons. ⤵ bit.ly/3PBORs7

For four years, a RAND project has counted the number of people living unsheltered in the Los Angeles neighborhoods of Hollywood, Venice, and Skid Row.

This new report contains updated findings and survey information: bit.ly/43n34MC

We're accepting applications for our new 1-year Master of Policy Analysis program at @RANDschooledu.

Apply now to join our first cohort this fall. ⬇️
bit.ly/4v1pA9X
Amid concerns about the diminishing role of reading full books in schools, this report examines whether middle and high school English teachers still assign them: bit.ly/4tCjsUq
Expert: Clearing the Strait of Hormuz of mines could be quick—if Iran isn't firing projectiles or sending out attack boats. But the effort could take months if that's not the case. bit.ly/4dnVpnn

New study: The overall number of unsheltered people in Hollywood, Skid Row, and Venice remained flat in 2025. But rough sleeping—sleeping without a tent, vehicle, or other shelter—rose by 20%, reaching its highest level in four years of monitoring. bit.ly/3PFgosH

International collaboration is a cornerstone of modern scientific research. But such collaborations can also be misused.

New paper on research security in science and technology: bit.ly/3RlFkGc
